CAFETERIA LESSON · CAFETERIA · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Chocolate Milk — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the tray’s most recognizable carton — named from across the room — and runs a gentle compare with its white cousin.

What is this?

Chocolate milk is milk mixed with cocoa and a little sugar, served in a small carton with the words printed on the front. It is the same white milk inside a brown costume.

What does it mean?

Name the drink asks for recall at a distance — the carton is recognizable across a whole cafeteria, which makes it the ideal first far-name game.

What does the child need to know?

Pair the two milk cards side by side and let the child tell them apart by color first, name second. The comparison does the teaching; the labels just confirm it.

Why this matters

Drinks are named before foods at this age — cartons are held daily, and a child who can name the drink can request it, which is real power.

What it teaches

Distance naming, color-based sorting, and same-but-different comparison.

Words to learn

chocolate milkmilkbrownwhitecartonsip

Say this to your child

“Two milk cartons! This one is brown — chocolate milk. This one is white — regular milk. Run and get the chocolate one! ... Now look: same box, different color. Sip and guess — which cup is which?”

Step by step

  1. Set the chocolate-milk card at one end of the table and the white milk card at the other. Name each one, then ask for them from across the room — run and fetch! Once fetched, compare the cartons: same shape, different colors. Pour a splash of each into clear cups and guess before tasting which is which.

Look closer at the picture

Watch the fetch: a child who runs to the correct card from across the room has done distance naming — the far end of the naming skill range.

Ask your child

Which one is chocolate milk? What color is each carton? Are the boxes the same shape? Which do you want today?

What your child can say or do

Choc milk! / Brown one! / Same box. / This one!

Out in the real world

School cafeterias hand out both milk cartons side by side every day — this lesson is rehearsal for a choice the child will make a thousand times.

Try it together

Milk mail: hide both cards in different rooms, then deliver letters — take the brown letter to the kitchen! Take the white one to the sofa! Fetching by name is the game.

Understanding check

Mix the two milk cards with a juice card and ask for chocolate milk. One correct grab, from any distance, passes.

This lesson pairs with the Chocolate Milk flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Cafeteria.
